record_identity.title: Absence of a bounded regulatory and independent-investigation evidence-access pathway

summary: A structural governance failure in which an AI governance framework preserves incident evidence, reporting duties or auditability in principle but does not establish a lawful, authority-verified, confidentiality-protected and auditable pathway through which an authorised regulator or properly mandated independent investigator can obtain the evidence necessary to investigate a serious incident, assess compliance, determine causal mechanisms or verify remediation.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Caelestis currently requires incident routing, evidence preservation, audit reconstruction, regulatory reporting, minimisation of unnecessary disclosure, confidentiality-aware handling, independent audit in limited assurance contexts and controlled movement of incident evidence across sovereign boundaries. Those controls do not collectively establish the missing general pathway. In particular, the source-authoritative auditability instrument expressly states that its qualification classes do not independently create disclosure or audit authority. Without an operational access pathway, preserved evidence may remain practically unavailable to a competent authority or properly mandated investigator, while confidentiality may be invoked as an undifferentiated barrier rather than a condition governing necessary access. CAM should recognise and operationalise authority arising under applicable law, court order, contract, appointment or other valid mandate; it should not purport to create, enlarge or substitute for statutory investigative power.
evidence_confidence: verified corpus gap and authoritative regulatory basis; no external incident asserted

source_records.author_or_publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union / EUR-Lex

source_records.deployment_context: Regulation of high-risk AI systems and general-purpose AI models in the European Union.
source_records.source_context: Articles 21, 73 to 78 and 91 to 92 recognise reasoned competent-authority requests for information and logs, serious-incident reporting, provider investigation and cooperation, preservation against incident-cause impairment, market-surveillance and fundamental-rights authority access, confidential handling, Commission information requests, independent experts and technical evaluation access. Article 78 requires protection of intellectual property, confidential business information and trade secrets, investigation and audit integrity, security interests, proceedings and classified information; it also limits collection to strictly necessary data and requires cybersecurity and deletion controls.
source_records.relevance_note: Authoritative regulatory basis showing that necessary authority access, provider cooperation, incident reporting, cause-preserving investigation and confidentiality safeguards are complementary requirements rather than alternatives.

contextual_relations.rationale: OBS-0026 records dependence created by provider-mediated external-evaluator access, confidential disclosure and publication terms. FM-0056 is distinct: it concerns the absence of a general lawful and bounded evidence-access pathway for competent authorities and properly mandated incident investigators. The observation is not required as an evidence origin for this governance-gap record.

failure_mode_definition: A failure mode in which an AI governance framework, provider compliance architecture, incident-response programme or assurance system fails to establish a lawful, bounded, confidentiality-protected and auditable pathway through which an authorised regulator or properly mandated independent investigator can obtain evidence necessary to investigate a serious AI incident, assess compliance, determine a causal mechanism or verify a remediation claim. The failure may persist even where the framework requires evidence preservation, incident reporting, auditability or public transparency in principle, if it does not operationalise authority verification, request scope, evidence custody, protected access, provider cooperation, justified withholding, review and traceability. The pathway must recognise authority arising under applicable law, court order, contract, appointment or other valid mandate; it must not allow an investigator to self-authorise or treat a private evaluator as possessing regulatory power.
failure_threshold: The threshold is met where: (1) a serious incident, material compliance question, disputed causal mechanism or remediation claim requires evidence not reasonably available through public material; (2) a competent regulator or properly mandated independent investigator has a valid basis to request or inspect necessary evidence; and (3) the governing framework provides no sufficiently defined route to authenticate that authority, specify purpose and scope, preserve and identify responsive material, produce or inspect it through a controlled mechanism, record access and transformations, resolve or independently review material withholding, and close or retain the access record. The pathway is not sufficient if confidentiality, trade secrets, personal information, legal privilege, cybersecurity, model security or sovereign boundaries are treated either as automatic grounds for total refusal or as reasons for unrestricted disclosure. A sufficient pathway may use necessity and proportionality tests, redaction, pseudonymisation, privilege or withholding logs, secure data rooms, on-premises inspection, cleared personnel, escrow, staged access, technical testing, confidentiality undertakings, access logging, retention and deletion limits, and competent review of withheld material. It need not require public release, source-code production in every case, disclosure beyond lawful authority, weakening of live security controls or transfer across a sovereign boundary without a valid legal and security basis.

review_history.review_outcome: A new failure-mode record is warranted. Existing records address provider-mediated external evaluation and adjacent oversight problems but not the absence of the pathway itself. The smallest accurate set is one FM supported directly by authoritative legal and corpus-review sources, with no new OBS, PROP or PATCH. Regulator and independent-investigator access remain one mechanism while their authority bases remain expressly separate.
